Definition: from a presumed equivalent of the Latin flagellum; to whip, i.e. lash as a public punishment:--scourge.
BiblicalUsage: Phragelloo means to scourge, to lash as a public punishment, and it appears twice, both times at the cross. Pilate, willing to content the people, releases Barabbas and delivers Jesus, when he has scourged Him, to be crucified.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the scourging is the price of pleasing the crowd: Pilate knows Jesus is innocent, and he has Him lashed anyway.
